contractBoundary.sourceText: Nothing here is built. Where this file names a library, it is a recommendation; where it names a message to the engine, it is the screens' side of the contract and the engine's owners agree the final shape.

desktopNavigation.purpose: See what needs you, how things stand, and what happened
Ask a question, look at saved answers, record decisions
Say yes or no to actions, and watch jobs
Look after the data and what it means
Make and send the papers other people ask for
Add what Chausar does not have
Set what Chausar may see, send, keep and do, and check what it did

screens.title: The frame
screens.purpose: holding every screen in one steady shape.

details.For: holding every screen in one steady shape.
details.Shows: the rail with the seven places, the page, the ask line, the status line. A sheet when a row is open.
details.You can: go to a place, open a row, close a sheet, ask.
details.States: wide, medium and narrow windows (main file, part 4). Read only. Locked.
details.Rules: only Today carries a count. One sheet at a time. The ask line and the status line are on every screen except first run and the lock screen.

screens.effectivePurpose: holding every screen in one steady shape.

screens.title: Lock screen
screens.purpose: keeping the books closed on a shared computer.

details.For: keeping the books closed on a shared computer.
details.Shows: the mark, the workspace name, one field, "Unlock". A link for Windows Hello or Touch ID where present. "Forgot it? Use your recovery kit." One line saying what is paused while locked.
details.You can: unlock, unlock with the computer's own check, open the recovery kit flow.
details.States: wrong passphrase (the field says so; no count of tries is shown). Too many tries (a wait, with the time). Locked by idle time, or by "Lock now".
details.Rules: nothing from the workspace is visible behind the lock. Keys and connector tokens are usable only while unlocked. Day 7 adds a second ask before a money action (WK-02).

screens.effectivePurpose: keeping the books closed on a shared computer.

screens.title: Banners
screens.purpose: telling the person that the whole app is in an unusual condition.

details.For: telling the person that the whole app is in an unusual condition.
details.Shows: a thin strip above the page: a few words and at most one button.
details.States: Chausar is driving; Demo clock; Read only; Sending is closed; Jobs are paused; Update needed; No connection. They stack in that order.
details.Rules: the Demo clock banner is on every screen, receipt and export while the test clock is in use. A real workspace can never show it. "Chausar is driving" stays for the whole session and its stop key ends the session within one second.

screens.effectivePurpose: telling the person that the whole app is in an unusual condition.

screens.title: The ask line
screens.purpose: asking a question, giving a task, or jumping to a thing, from any screen.

schedule.sourceText: Day 1; the suggestions grow with the menu on day 2 and day 5.

details.For: asking a question, giving a task, or jumping to a thing, from any screen.
details.Shows: your square, the field ("Ask a question, or give a task"), the microphone, "Ctrl K".
details.You can: type and press Enter; hold the microphone or Ctrl Space to talk; pick a suggestion.
details.States: empty. Typing: up to five suggestions, each with its kind in small type (calculation, customer, place, saved answer). About something: when you ask from a customer's page the line shows "About: Kiran Retail Demo" with a way to clear it. Listening. Reading back an amount or a date (SH-05). Choosing a calculation: the line says so in words. No model connected: "No AI model connected. Pick a calculation from the menu." and the menu opens. Waiting for the network. Read only: questions work, tasks say who holds the pen.
details.Rules: a question goes to Ask. A task becomes a prepared action and opens its approval sheet; nothing runs from the ask line alone. What is typed is data: text pasted from a file or a message cannot give Chausar an order.

screens.effectivePurpose: asking a question, giving a task, or jumping to a thing, from any screen.

screens.title: Talking to it
screens.purpose: asking by voice, in Hindi, English or a mix.

schedule.sourceText: Day 1; more speech providers compared on day 8.

details.For: asking by voice, in Hindi, English or a mix.
details.Shows: while you hold the key, the words as they are heard. Then the question as text. Any amount or date heard is shown back large: "₹2,00,000. Is that right?" with Yes and Change.
details.You can: confirm, change the text, or drop a recorded voice note onto the ask line.
details.States: voice is off (the microphone opens Trust, Rules, Send, where it can be switched on). Paid speech in use: the cost per minute is shown beside the microphone. Local speech in use: "on this computer". Could not hear: "Not sure what was said." and the words that were caught.
details.Rules: voice is off by default. The intent is always confirmed as text before anything runs. "Do lakh" is shown as ₹2,00,000. A sentence that ends in "nahi" changes the meaning, and the text shown must reflect it. No raw audio is kept. When Send is set to nothing or shape only, speech is turned into text on this computer.

screens.effectivePurpose: asking by voice, in Hindi, English or a mix.

screens.title: Workspace, view and language
screens.purpose: switching between businesses, and choosing how the app looks and reads.

details.For: switching between businesses, and choosing how the app looks and reads.
details.Shows: a small menu at the foot of the rail: the workspaces you have a seat in, each marked demo or real; the three views; the languages; Lock now; About this build.
details.States: one workspace only (no list). A demo workspace (the word "demo" after its name, always).
details.Rules: each workspace has its own key; nothing is read across workspaces. A workspace is marked demo or real when it is made, and the mark never changes.

screens.effectivePurpose: switching between businesses, and choosing how the app looks and reads.

screens.title: The tray icon and background mode
screens.purpose: keeping jobs running when the window is closed.

details.For: keeping jobs running when the window is closed.
details.Shows: a small icon in the system tray with the count of things awaiting your review. Its menu: Open Chausar, Pause jobs, Quit.
details.States: background mode off: closing the window stops the engine, and the next start shows "Jobs were paused while Chausar was closed". Start at login: off by default.
details.Rules: scheduled jobs on the free app run only while this computer is awake. The app says so where the setting is.

screens.effectivePurpose: keeping jobs running when the window is closed.

screens.title: Updates
screens.purpose: staying on a safe build without losing data.

schedule.sourceText: Day 1 (updater, preview expiry), day 3 (an old install updates itself), day 10 (hardened).

details.For: staying on a safe build without losing data.
details.Shows: in Trust, Vault: the version, the channel, the date the preview expires, "Check now". When an update is ready: one row on Today, "Update ready. Your data is saved first." with Update.
details.States: updating (the steps in words: saving a copy, updating, checking). Rolled back: "The update did not finish. Your data is as it was." An older build meets a newer vault: "This build is older than your vault. Update Chausar to open it." and nothing is written. Release withdrawn: the Update needed banner. Mac not yet signed: "This Mac build cannot update itself yet. Download the new one."
details.Rules: a running job finishes or is paused and resumed across an update. The update check is the only call the app makes by itself, and Trust, Network lists it.

screens.effectivePurpose: staying on a safe build without losing data.

screens.title: Sign in again, and a route that is down
screens.purpose: telling the person plainly that the AI model cannot be reached, and why.

details.For: telling the person plainly that the AI model cannot be reached, and why.
details.Shows: one row where the answer would be: "Your Codex tool is signed out. Sign in again." with a button that starts the tool's own sign-in.
details.States: signed out; not installed; version not tested; timed out; chat only, no calculations.
details.Rules: never a silent retry and never an automatic switch to another route. The person may try the next route in their own order, and that is a new visible attempt with its own receipt. The app never reads or stores a subscription token.

screens.effectivePurpose: telling the person plainly that the AI model cannot be reached, and why.

screens.title: Opening a link
screens.purpose: stopping a link in an answer or a file from opening on its own.

details.For: stopping a link in an answer or a file from opening on its own.
details.Shows: a small dialog with the full address as text, "Open in your browser" and Cancel.
details.Rules: answers and imported text are drawn as plain content: no remote images, no raw HTML. The app window never goes to another page.

screens.effectivePurpose: stopping a link in an answer or a file from opening on its own.

screens.title: Reporting a fault
screens.purpose: telling Chausar's makers about a fault without sending any business data.

schedule.sourceText: Day 1 (crash report on request), day 10 (fault report).

details.For: telling Chausar's makers about a fault without sending any business data.
details.Shows: the whole report as text before it goes anywhere: app version, operating system, kinds of events, route health, error codes. A line at the top: "No names, amounts, file names, cell values or questions are in this report."
details.You can: save it as a file and send it yourself. After a crash: Send report, or Don't send.
details.Rules: nothing is sent unless the person presses Send report. No telemetry by default.

screens.effectivePurpose: telling Chausar's makers about a fault without sending any business data.

screens.title: Help
screens.purpose: looking up a key, a word, or what works with no internet.

schedule.sourceText: Day 1 (keys, what works without internet), day 10 (word list).

details.For: looking up a key, a word, or what works with no internet.
details.Shows: three short lists in a sheet: the keys, the word list in plain words, and what works with no internet and what waits.

screens.effectivePurpose: looking up a key, a word, or what works with no internet.

screens.title: A part that is not built yet
screens.purpose: being honest while the app is built in public.

details.For: being honest while the app is built in public.
details.Shows: where the screen would be: "Not built yet. This arrives on day 7." and which part is missing.
details.Rules: a feature that is shown working once but not yet tested on the bench carries the label experimental on its own screen.

screens.effectivePurpose: being honest while the app is built in public.

screens.title: Welcome
screens.purpose: three choices before anything else.

details.For: three choices before anything else.
details.Shows: the language (English, हिंदी), the view as three small live drawings (Simple, Guided, Books), and "I have a business" or "I have an idea".
details.States: a workspace already exists on this computer: "Open Demo shop" comes first. "Try the demo shop" opens a demo workspace.
details.Rules: nothing is stored until the vault exists.

screens.effectivePurpose: three choices before anything else.

screens.title: Business identity card and GST mode
screens.purpose: telling Chausar which business this is.

details.For: telling Chausar which business this is.
details.Shows: six optional fields, each on its own line: PAN, GSTIN, Udyam number, CIN, food licence, import-export code. Then the GST mode as three rows: regular, composition, not registered.
details.States: a field with the wrong format says which part is wrong ("A GSTIN has 15 characters"). Nothing is looked up online, and the screen says so.
details.Rules: format checks only. Every report later says which GST modes it applies to.

screens.effectivePurpose: telling Chausar which business this is.

screens.title: Create the vault
screens.purpose: locking the books before anything is read.

details.For: locking the books before anything is read.
details.Shows: the workspace name, the passphrase twice, an optional PIN for quick unlock, and the result of the disk check: "This disk is encrypted" or "This disk is not encrypted. Chausar encrypts its own files. Turning on BitLocker protects the rest."
details.States: passphrase too short. Linux with no safe keyring: "This computer has no safe place for a key. Chausar will ask for the passphrase each time."

screens.effectivePurpose: locking the books before anything is read.

screens.title: Recovery kit
screens.purpose: a way back in when the passphrase is forgotten or the laptop is lost.

details.For: a way back in when the passphrase is forgotten or the laptop is lost.
details.Shows: the code, large, in groups of four. Three lines: where the key lives, how recovery works, how to open the vault on a new computer. Print. A tick box: "I have kept this code somewhere safe."
details.States: shown once. Continue is not available until the box is ticked.
details.Rules: printed in Hindi and English on one page. The screen keeps the code only until the box is ticked.

screens.effectivePurpose: a way back in when the passphrase is forgotten or the laptop is lost.

screens.title: Connect an AI model
screens.purpose: choosing how Chausar reaches an AI model, or choosing none for now.

details.For: choosing how Chausar reaches an AI model, or choosing none for now.
details.Shows: one row per route with its health and a short note: your own Codex tool, your own Claude Code tool, an API key, a local model on this computer. Under them: the send level the app starts with (shape only) and that voice is off.
details.You can: connect a route, set the order you want them tried in, skip.
details.States: ready, signed out, not installed, error. Skipped: "No model yet. Importing, the menu of calculations, receipts and backup work without one."
details.Rules: the app starts your own installed tool and never handles its sign-in. The managed allowance is shown as "planned, not available yet".

screens.effectivePurpose: choosing how Chausar reaches an AI model, or choosing none for now.

screens.title: Pick a starter pack
screens.purpose: starting from ready-made meanings for your kind of business.

details.For: starting from ready-made meanings for your kind of business.
details.Shows: the kinds of business as rows. A pack that is not checked says "draft, not yet checked".
details.You can: pick one, or "Start from a conversation".

screens.effectivePurpose: starting from ready-made meanings for your kind of business.

screens.title: Bring a file
screens.purpose: getting the first data in.

schedule.sourceText: Day 1 (sheets), day 3 (bank statement PDF), day 4 (Tally, Zoho Books, GST files).

details.For: getting the first data in.
details.Shows: after you pick a file: its name, the first rows as plain text, and the recipe Chausar would use, with its state. For a layout it does not know: "Pick your columns", one row per column with a choice of date, customer, amount, invoice, or ignore.
details.You can: confirm the columns, give a PDF's password, bring another file.
details.States: password needed ("Used once, on this computer. Not kept."). Result: "214 rows taken, 3 flagged, 2 refused", each group opening its rows and reasons. Refused whole: the reason from the fixed list, and where the refused file is kept. A scanned statement with no text: "This statement is a picture. Chausar cannot read it yet."
details.Rules: cell text is shown as data. Each column choice is logged as a decision. A file is labelled "file", never shown as a live connection.

screens.effectivePurpose: getting the first data in.

screens.title: Agree what your words mean
screens.purpose: accepting or changing what Chausar proposes, with the evidence in front of you.

details.For: accepting or changing what Chausar proposes, with the evidence in front of you.
details.Shows: the six steps across the top. "Agree what your words mean", with how many are done. One row per proposal: the word, the proposed meaning, its state. The open row shows the evidence as a thin bar ("398 of 412 past invoices fit") with Accept and Change. At the bottom: what is blocked, and that nothing has left this computer.
details.States: a proposal that needs an answer (filled amber, "needs your answer"). All accepted: Continue. Checks failed: the row says which check and what would fix it.
details.Rules: the setup guide proposes and never accepts. Only your click accepts. It asks at most three questions to finish a source.

screens.effectivePurpose: accepting or changing what Chausar proposes, with the evidence in front of you.

screens.title: The first answer
screens.purpose: ending setup with proof that it works.

schedule.sourceText: Day 1, and from the dictionary on day 2.

details.For: ending setup with proof that it works.
details.Shows: one suggested question as a button. Then the answer page (AS-04) with the receipt open.
details.Rules: the time from the first screen to this receipt is measured.

screens.effectivePurpose: ending setup with proof that it works.

screens.title: The sharing question
screens.purpose: asking, once and plainly, whether you want to share anything with Chausar.

details.For: asking, once and plainly, whether you want to share anything with Chausar.
details.Shows: after the first receipt: two boxes that start empty, "Setup shapes" and "Your corrections", and one sentence: "Your books also hold other people's details. Those never leave this computer." A link opens the exact file that would be sent.
details.You can: tick, or leave empty and continue.
details.Rules: never shown at install. No feature depends on any box. Full screen: TR-11.

screens.effectivePurpose: asking, once and plainly, whether you want to share anything with Chausar.

screens.title: An idea, not a business yet
screens.purpose: a founder who has an idea and no books.

details.For: a founder who has an idea and no books.
details.Shows: a conversation on the left and, on the right, the draft as it forms: the business in a few lines, the money for one sale, a first 90-day plan, and the unknowns. Every line carries a small label: told by owner, or assumption.
details.States: a number nobody gave is left blank and listed under unknowns, or shown as a range with its source and date once a pack provides one.
details.Rules: the AI model writes no number.

screens.effectivePurpose: a founder who has an idea and no books.

screens.title: Setup checklist
screens.purpose: the steps to make the business legal and ready.

schedule.sourceText: Day 1; more kinds of business on day 5.

details.For: the steps to make the business legal and ready.
details.Shows: rows: kind of entity, registration, bank account, the GST decision, Udyam, licences. Each row names its rule, the source and the date it was checked.
details.Rules: the list comes from a dated rule table, never from the AI model. Filing is handed to a provider; the app does not file.

screens.effectivePurpose: the steps to make the business legal and ready.

screens.title: Open a vault with the recovery kit
screens.purpose: getting back in on this or a new computer.

details.For: getting back in on this or a new computer.
details.Shows: a field for the code, and "Choose your backup file" on a new computer.
details.States: wrong code. Backup older than the last use: "This backup is from 28 September. Anything after that is not in it."
details.Rules: after a restore, sending stays closed until every action in the gap is checked (WK-15).

screens.effectivePurpose: getting back in on this or a new computer.

screens.title: Join a workspace from another computer
screens.purpose: adding a second machine or a second person.

details.For: adding a second machine or a second person.
details.Shows: on the new computer, a short code. On a computer already in, the same code to compare, with Approve.
details.States: the invite expired (15 minutes) or was used.

screens.effectivePurpose: adding a second machine or a second person.

screens.title: Today, Guided view
screens.purpose: seeing in ten seconds what needs you and how things stand.

schedule.sourceText: Day 1 (rows, earlier today), day 5 (charts, worth a look, the week ahead), day 7 (Review). Picture: S01.

details.For: seeing in ten seconds what needs you and how things stand.
details.Shows: the date. "Awaiting your review" with its count, and up to four rows. "This month": three small charts, each a label, a figure, what changed, and the picture. "Earlier today": up to six marks on one line.
details.You can: open a row in place to see one more line and Review; open a chart's receipt; open the full activity list.
details.States: nothing awaits: "Nothing awaits your review." and the charts move up. More than four: "See all 7". Setup not finished: a first row, "Setup: step 5 of 6". An update is ready: a row. No data yet: the charts say "not loaded yet" and the due dates still show.
details.Worth a look: Below the review rows, up to five rows of things that changed or are due: a figure that moved, a due date within seven days, a decision due for review, a refused file, a brief that was built late, what was missed while the computer slept. Review rows and worth-a-look rows together never show more than five at rest. Each opens its receipt or its page. From day 7 a row may offer Prepare.
details.Rules: the three charts are chosen by the starter pack and can be changed. A figure that moved and has no measured cause yet says so; it never offers a cause as fact.

screens.effectivePurpose: seeing in ten seconds what needs you and how things stand.

screens.title: Today, Simple view
screens.purpose: a shop owner: what needs a yes, and today's cash.

details.For: a shop owner: what needs a yes, and today's cash.
details.Shows: the same rows, taller and in larger type. "Today's cash sales" with one field and Enter. The week's cash as seven bars.
details.You can: hold to talk; say or type the day's cash.
details.States: today's cash not entered (the bar for today is open). Entered: the bar fills and the row says "told by owner".
details.Rules: the cash figure is stored as something the owner said, not as a fact from the books. Receipts for a period with no cash entry say "cash sales not captured".

screens.effectivePurpose: a shop owner: what needs a yes, and today's cash.

screens.title: Today, Books view
screens.purpose: an accountant: the queue, and how far the month's close has got.

schedule.sourceText: Day 1 (table), day 4 to 6 (the close). Picture: S15.

details.For: an accountant: the queue, and how far the month's close has got.
details.Shows: "Awaiting your review" as a table: what, party or account, as written in the source, amount, since, then (who decides). "September close": bank reconciliation, purchases against GSTR-2B, TDS against Form 26AS, trial balance, each with its state and an action.
details.States: an item this seat may prepare and not approve says "the owner approves".
details.Rules: arrow keys move, Enter opens. The status line says so.

screens.effectivePurpose: an accountant: the queue, and how far the month's close has got.

screens.title: Activity
screens.purpose: reading everything that happened, in order.

schedule.sourceText: Day 1; cost per step and a view per record on day 8.

details.For: reading everything that happened, in order.
details.Shows: a time line down the page, newest first. One sentence per step, with its square, its time, who acted, and its cost in rupees where it had one.
details.You can: filter by state, by person, by job, by day. Open any line to its proof: a receipt, an action's record, a request to the AI model.
details.States: the six step states of part 7 of the main file.
details.Rules: each sentence is built by the screen from a typed event, in Hindi or English. The engine sends no prose.

screens.effectivePurpose: reading everything that happened, in order.

screens.title: The ask page
screens.purpose: starting a question when you do not know what to ask.

schedule.sourceText: Day 1 (a small hand-written menu, labelled seed), day 2 (the menu from the dictionary), day 5 (the full set).

details.For: starting a question when you do not know what to ask.
details.Shows: "Ask", and the menu of calculations as rows grouped by topic: sales, collections, cash, stock, tax. Each row names the calculation and what it needs.
details.States: the day 1 menu says "seed" on the page and on every receipt. No model connected: the menu is the way to ask, and the period is chosen from a plain calendar.

screens.effectivePurpose: starting a question when you do not know what to ask.

screens.title: What Chausar understood
screens.purpose: seeing which calculation was chosen before it runs.

details.For: seeing which calculation was chosen before it runs.
details.Shows: one line under the question: the calculation, the period, and who is counted. "Invoiced by customer · August 2026." A Change link.
details.You can: change the calculation, the period or the group, each from a short list.
details.Rules: your correction is logged as structure only. "Last month" follows the workspace's calendar and its April to March year.

screens.effectivePurpose: seeing which calculation was chosen before it runs.

screens.title: One question back
screens.purpose: settling a question that could mean two things.

details.For: settling a question that could mean two things.
details.Shows: "Which did you mean?" and the choices as rows, each with one line saying how it differs: "Billed: invoices raised. Received: money in the bank. Earned: after returns."
details.Rules: exactly one question. If the answer does not settle it, the result is Not yet.

screens.effectivePurpose: settling a question that could mean two things.

screens.title: An answer
screens.purpose: the number, and everything it must admit.

details.For: the number, and everything it must admit.
details.Shows: the question as the title. The line from AS-02. One big figure with a few words beside it ("14 customers"). Ranked bars or a chart. One line: "Checked against the receipt. 214 rows, 3 left out." Save, and Save as a check.
details.States: part of the data missing: the figure for what is loaded, and "3 months not loaded yet" in words. A written explanation that failed the number guard: the explanation is removed and one line says "The explanation was removed: a number in it was not on the receipt." Rows may not be sent to the model: the explanation is written from a template and says so. Two meanings give two numbers: both are shown as different measures, each with its own receipt, never as an error. Stale: the date and Rebuild.
details.Rules: no number on this page is typed by the AI model. Every figure and every bar opens the receipt.

screens.effectivePurpose: the number, and everything it must admit.

screens.title: The receipt
screens.purpose: checking a number.

schedule.sourceText: Day 1; two dates on day 3; versions on day 4; the rule that allowed it on day 6.

details.For: checking a number.
details.Shows: the six parts listed in part 6 of the main file.
details.You can: open the rows, export, open what was sent to the AI model, open the meaning, open the recipe.
details.States: from a seed menu: "seed". Recipe not yet tested: "not yet tested". An amount with no exchange rate: "not counted", with the count. As known on a past date: both dates. Sent through your own Codex or Claude Code tool: "Only the text handed to the tool is visible." Demo clock: the label.
details.Rules: the receipt names the recipe, its state and who accepted it. It carries five version numbers in its small print.

screens.effectivePurpose: checking a number.

screens.title: The rows behind a number
screens.purpose: seeing every row that was counted, and every row that was left out.

details.For: seeing every row that was counted, and every row that was left out.
details.Shows: a full-page table: file, row number, the cells as written, the amount. Two tabs of words: counted, left out.
details.States: rows hidden from this seat: a line says how many and why.

screens.effectivePurpose: seeing every row that was counted, and every row that was left out.

screens.title: What was sent to the AI model
screens.purpose: seeing the exact words that left the computer for one answer.

details.For: seeing the exact words that left the computer for one answer.
details.Shows: the request as plain text, with stand-ins where names, phone numbers and GSTINs were ("CUSTOMER_1"). The route, the send level, the size, the cost.
details.States: kept for the time you set, then only its digest: "The text was removed after 30 days. Its fingerprint is kept."

screens.effectivePurpose: seeing the exact words that left the computer for one answer.

screens.title: Not yet
screens.purpose: an honest stop when no calculation fits.

details.For: an honest stop when no calculation fits.
details.Shows: "Not yet. No calculation covers this." The reason in one line, for example "no peer data exists yet" or "needs data: the GST file for September". "It is on the wanted list."
details.You can: pick a nearby calculation from a short list; pack the question for a person (RP-08).
details.Rules: never a guess.

screens.effectivePurpose: an honest stop when no calculation fits.

screens.title: Stopped by a rule
screens.purpose: saying which rule stopped an answer.

schedule.sourceText: Day 1; seats and markings on day 6.

details.For: saying which rule stopped an answer.
details.Shows: the rule in plain words ("Anything marked confidential is hidden from the cofounder seat") and who can change it.

screens.effectivePurpose: saying which rule stopped an answer.

screens.title: Why did it change
screens.purpose: understanding a movement without mistaking a guess for a fact.

details.For: understanding a movement without mistaking a guess for a fact.
details.Shows: the title as a finding ("Collections fell 18% in September"). "Measured": a bridge chart from the earlier figure to the later one, each bar a measured cause with its amount. "Possible causes", labelled Guess: rows with an open amber square and the evidence for and against. Record a decision, and Save.
details.States: long investigations show their plan as steps and can be resumed. An investigation reopened later checks your permissions again. A guess that cites something from outside names its source and when it was fetched.
details.Rules: the two parts are never merged. Nothing from outside enters a measured number.

screens.effectivePurpose: understanding a movement without mistaking a guess for a fact.

screens.title: What if
screens.purpose: trying a change in an assumption without touching the books.

details.For: trying a change in an assumption without touching the books.
details.Shows: the label "What if" beside the title. The assumption changed, as before and after. Two figures side by side: your books, and with the change.
details.Rules: a what-if has no way to write to facts. Its receipt says "What if".

screens.effectivePurpose: using a tool made for other assistants, safely.

screens.effectivePurpose: a question a tool asks you, kept apart from everything else.

screens.effectivePurpose: letting another AI assistant ask Chausar for numbers with receipts.

screens.purpose: what reaches your phone.

details.For: what reaches your phone.
details.Shows: WhatsApp and mail, each a row with its switch; the exact text of each message; your agreement with its date; messages this month against 30; the cost of each; which kinds of change may be approved from the phone.

screens.effectivePurpose: what reaches your phone.

screens.purpose: more languages, starting with Hinglish.

details.For: more languages, starting with Hinglish.

screens.effectivePurpose: more languages, starting with Hinglish.

screens.title: Rules
screens.purpose: the four questions on one screen.

details.For: the four questions on one screen.
details.Shows: four rows, See, Send, Keep, Do, each with its setting in a few words. A row opens in place. Under them, "What left this computer today" as a small drawing.
details.Rules: software enforces each rule before anything happens. Only the owner may change Send and the sharing boxes.

screens.effectivePurpose: the four questions on one screen.

screens.title: See
screens.purpose: which sources Chausar may read, and which data is marked.

details.For: which sources Chausar may read, and which data is marked.
details.Shows: each source with No and Yes. From day 6: the markings personal, financial and confidential, and what each seat may see.
details.Rules: a marking follows the data into every summary, report, brief and export made from it. Bank data is marked financial from the start.

screens.effectivePurpose: which sources Chausar may read, and which data is marked.

screens.title: Send
screens.purpose: what an AI model may be sent.

schedule.sourceText: Day 1; the rule for financial data on day 6.

details.For: what an AI model may be sent.
details.Shows: three levels, each drawn as a tiny table of your own data: nothing, shape only (headings and types, no values), samples (a few rows). The level in use has an ink line above it. Under them: voice (off, and "audio leaves this computer when voice is on"), and "Local only" as a named setting.
details.Rules: names, phone numbers and GSTINs are swapped for stand-ins before any call and put back after. Data marked financial goes only to a local model or a route you approved.

screens.effectivePurpose: what an AI model may be sent.

screens.title: Keep
screens.purpose: what is kept, and for how long.

schedule.sourceText: Day 1; keep-until per kind on day 6.

details.For: what is kept, and for how long.
details.Shows: rows per kind of data with how long it is kept. A link to the list of everything the app writes to disk.

screens.effectivePurpose: what is kept, and for how long.

screens.title: Do
screens.purpose: what may run without asking.

schedule.sourceText: Day 1 (the presets, stored), day 7 (actions), day 8 (the full screen).

details.For: what may run without asking.
details.Shows: three presets: ask me everything (the start), routine work on its own, everything that is allowed. Then each kind of action as a row with its switch and its daily limits on count and amount. Then "Always waits for you", a list with no switches: money, messages to outsiders, deleting, prices, stock, listings, sharing, invites to outsiders, tax filings.
details.States: from day 8, beside each kind: how often the rule would have agreed with what you approved.

screens.effectivePurpose: what may run without asking.

screens.title: People
screens.purpose: who is in, and what each may do.

details.For: who is in, and what each may do.
details.Shows: rows: the person, the seat, what the seat allows in a few words. Invite.
details.You can: invite a cofounder, an accountant (reads, prepares, cannot approve money), a CA (reads and exports, until a date), staff (adds entries, sees their own). "Invite my accountant" also makes a one-page guide to forward. Remove a person.
details.States: a CA seat past its end date. Removed: "Removed on 2 Oct. What was already copied or exported stays with that person."

screens.effectivePurpose: who is in, and what each may do.

screens.title: Machines and the pen
screens.purpose: which computers hold this workspace, and which one may write.

details.For: which computers hold this workspace, and which one may write.
details.Shows: a small drawing: the computer that holds the pen, the shared folder of locked files, the other computers that read, and the phone. "Hand over the pen."
details.States: this computer is read only. Taking the pen when the holder cannot be reached: experimental, and late changes from the old holder are shown for a person to settle.
details.Rules: one writer at a time. Only the computer that holds the pen runs scheduled jobs.

screens.effectivePurpose: which computers hold this workspace, and which one may write.

screens.title: Models
screens.purpose: each route to an AI model, its terms and its cost.

details.For: each route to an AI model, its terms and its cost.

details.States: chat only, no calculations. Answers only, not for actions. From day 8: the same test for every route, as a table.

screens.effectivePurpose: each route to an AI model, its terms and its cost.

screens.title: Network
screens.purpose: every call that left this computer.

schedule.sourceText: Day 1; taint and plugins on day 8 and 9.

details.For: every call that left this computer.

details.You can: filter by plugin.
details.States: a send stopped because the run had read outside text: the exact content that would have gone, waiting for you.

screens.effectivePurpose: every call that left this computer.

screens.title: Record
screens.purpose: who did what, when and why, in a form that shows tampering.

details.For: who did what, when and why, in a form that shows tampering.
details.Shows: a time line: who, what, the rule in plain words, when, which computer. Filters by person and day. Verify.
details.States: verified, or the line where the chain breaks. One sentence states the limit: "This record shows tampering. It cannot stop the owner of a computer from wiping that computer."

screens.effectivePurpose: who did what, when and why, in a form that shows tampering.

screens.title: Sharing
screens.purpose: what you share with Chausar, if you share.

details.For: what you share with Chausar, if you share.
details.Shows: the boxes, each empty at the start. The exact file that would be sent. "What I shared": each batch with its date, size and count, Open and Delete from the server, and a running line: "412 events shared, 0 names, 0 amounts." Credits, under a public name or none.
details.States: a batch blocked on this computer because a GSTIN, PAN, phone or mail was found in it: the line is shown. Sharing withdrawn.
details.Rules: structure only. Never values, names or amounts.

screens.effectivePurpose: what you share with Chausar, if you share.

screens.title: Vault
screens.purpose: looking after the one copy of the books.

details.For: looking after the one copy of the books.
details.Shows: the last backup and whether its test restore passed; Back up now; Restore; the lock (idle time, PIN, the computer's own check); the disk check; the version (SH-08).

screens.effectivePurpose: looking after the one copy of the books.

screens.title: Delete, and the deletion report
screens.purpose: deleting something everywhere, with proof.

details.For: deleting something everywhere, with proof.
details.Shows: after a deletion, a table: each place data lives, and for each: deleted, pending, or not possible, with the reason. "Not possible" names outside copies honestly: the AI provider for its stated period, briefs already sent, old versions in your Drive.
details.You can: export the report.
details.Rules: nothing is reported deleted without a check that it is gone. A restore keeps deleted things deleted.

screens.effectivePurpose: deleting something everywhere, with proof.

screens.title: What the paid plan can see
screens.purpose: two promises kept apart.

schedule.sourceText: Day 6; the plan's state on day 10.

details.For: two promises kept apart.
details.Shows: "Hosted backup and sync are blind: the server holds only locked files and no key." "Hosted jobs are not blind: the server holds a key for that one job while it works." Each hosted job is listed with its switch. Every paid part says "planned, not available yet".
details.States: the plan ended: "Your plan ended. Your data is here and nothing is locked."

screens.effectivePurpose: two promises kept apart.

screens.title: The privacy notice and your agreements
screens.purpose: reading what you agreed to, and taking it back.

details.For: reading what you agreed to, and taking it back.
details.Shows: the notice in Hindi and English. Each agreement by person and purpose with its date. Withdraw.

screens.effectivePurpose: reading what you agreed to, and taking it back.

screens.title: Messages
screens.purpose: knowing something is ready without opening the laptop.

schedule.sourceText: Day 5 (the week ahead), day 9 (approvals). Picture: S16.

details.For: knowing something is ready without opening the laptop.
details.Shows: four fixed messages: the week ahead is ready; something awaits your review; a document was received; a due date is near.
details.States: a small change that can be undone: Approve, Not now, Open the app. Anything else: Open the app only.
details.Rules: no amounts, no names. Each button works once, for the owner's number only, and expires after 30 minutes. A forwarded copy does nothing. About 30 messages a month.

screens.effectivePurpose: knowing something is ready without opening the laptop.

screens.title: The link page
screens.purpose: getting from a message to the app.

details.For: getting from a message to the app.
details.Shows: the wordmark and one line: "Open Chausar on your computer to see this." If the app is on this device, it opens.
details.States: the link is old or was changed: "This link no longer works."
details.Rules: the page holds no data.

screens.effectivePurpose: getting from a message to the app.

screens.title: Mail
screens.purpose: the same messages by mail, as the fallback.

details.For: the same messages by mail, as the fallback.

screens.effectivePurpose: the same messages by mail, as the fallback.

screens.title: The phone page
screens.purpose: a calmer way to see what awaits you, away from the desk.

schedule.sourceText: After day 10, for the founder's decision. Picture: S17.

details.For: a calmer way to see what awaits you, away from the desk.
details.Shows: "Awaiting your review" as rows, with Approve only on what the phone may approve; "The week ahead" as three headlines; when the laptop was last seen.
details.Rules: headlines only. Figures and receipts stay on the computer.

screens.effectivePurpose: a calmer way to see what awaits you, away from the desk.

screens.purpose: forwarding a bill or a statement to Chausar.

details.Rules: a forwarded document is data. It enters the same checks as a file brought on the computer, and nothing is stored before you confirm.

screens.effectivePurpose: forwarding a bill or a statement to Chausar.

commonStates.text:
## 10. States every screen must handle

Every screen is designed for these states, with these words. A screen's own special states are in the Screens file.

| State | What the person sees |
|---|---|
| First use, nothing here yet | One line that says what will be here, and one action. "Nothing awaits your review." "No sources yet. Add a source." |
| Loading | The frame at once. What was known last time, with its time. The status line says what is being read. No spinner |
| Ready | The screen as drawn |
| Partly loaded | The numbers that exist, and "not loaded yet" in words for the rest. The coverage line says what is missing |
| No change | "No change since Monday." This is different from not knowing |
| Not enough to tell | "Not enough loaded to tell. 3 months are not loaded yet." With the action that would fix it |
| Stale | The old result with its date and the label stale. A Rebuild link |
| Not yet | "Not yet. No calculation covers this." What was asked is added to the wanted list |
| Stopped by a rule | The name of the rule in plain words, and who can change it |
| Failed | What happened, what it means, what to do. A code in small type. Never the raw error text |
| Waiting for the network | The step shows an open green square and "waiting for the network". Work that needs no network carries on |
| Read only | A banner. Buttons that change things are not shown; the page says who holds the pen |
| Hidden from this seat | "Some rows are hidden from your seat." If showing a total would reveal fewer than three hidden rows, the total is refused with that reason |
| Locked | The lock screen |
| Feature not built yet | During the ten days, a screen whose engine part is missing says which part and which day brings it |

phone.text:
## 12. The phone

![What reaches the phone, and what never does](2026-10-01-chausar-app-frontend/diagrams/phone.svg)

The desktop is the engine. In the ten days the phone gets three things.

1. **Messages** by WhatsApp and mail, from fixed templates: the week ahead is ready; something awaits your review; a document was received; a due date is near. A message is a headline and a link. It never carries an amount or a name.
2. **Simple approvals.** A message about a small change that stays inside your workspace and can be undone has three buttons: Approve, Not now, Open the app. A message about money, an outside message, deleting or anything that cannot be undone has one: Open the app. Each button works once and expires after 30 minutes.
3. **The link page.** The link opens a plain page that holds no data and hands over to the app on your computer. A changed or expired link opens nothing.

![What a message says](2026-10-01-chausar-app-frontend/pictures/S16-Phone-Messages.light.png)

Free text sent to the number gets one fixed reply with a link to the app, and the words "Reply HELP for a person, STOP to end messages". Tools, Phone shows what is switched on, the exact text of each message before the first one is sent, your opt-in, how many messages went this month against the budget of 30, and what each cost.

After day 10 the phone can get a page of its own, paired to the desktop: the list of what is awaiting your review, simple approvals, and the week ahead as headlines. Figures and receipts stay on the computer. This page is drawn so the design is ready; whether and when to build it is the founder's decision.

![The paired phone page, proposed for after day 10](2026-10-01-chausar-app-frontend/pictures/S17-Phone-Page.light.png)

enterpriseNavigation.text:
## 3. Sub-places the enterprise version adds

| Place | Desktop sub-places | Added for a company |
|---|---|---|
| Today | Today, Activity | The lens. A leader's and an operator's form of Today |
| Ask | New, Saved, Decisions, Checks, Not yet | **Plans**: several options compared against one baseline, and the list of plans that compete for the same stock, budget or capacity |
| Work | Approvals, Jobs, Actions, What it can do | **Cases**: one record per piece of business work, with owner, deadline and state. **Agents**: the AI workers, what each may do, and its released version |
| Books | Sources, Meanings, Accounts, Customers, History, Memory | Customers becomes **Records**, for every kind of record. **Issues**: data that could not be published, with an owner. **Companies**: the group and how it combines |
| Reports | Packs, The week ahead, Due dates, Exports | The week ahead becomes **Briefs**, one per role. **Sent**: what was shared outward, with whom, and what can still be taken back |
| Tools | Small apps, Plugins, Other assistants, Phone | **Planning**: forecast and planning set-ups and whether each is still good to use. Phone moves to Trust as Channels |
| Trust | Rules, People, Models, Network, Record, Sharing, Vault | **Access**: roles, grants, reviews. **Markings**. **Retention**: every copy and its clock, and legal holds. **Channels**: what may be sent, as whom |
| Company | | **Sign-in**, **Health**, **Recovery**, **Keys**, **Support access**, **Computers**, **Quality**, **Build**, **Licence** |

Trust is about the data and what Chausar may do with it. Company is about the installation.

enterpriseParts.text:
## 4. New parts the enterprise version needs

Everything in the enterprise version is built from the parts of the desktop app. Twelve things are new.

| Part | What it is |
|---|---|
| Lens | A row of words; the chosen one is underlined |
| Approval chain | In an approval sheet, one small square per approver on a line, with the name under each: filled ink for a person who approved, open ink for the one whose turn it is, grey for those not reached. The rules are stated in words: "Two of three must approve. You cannot approve your own request." |
| Hidden content | When a role may know that something is hidden: "Some rows are hidden from your role", and a field shows the word "hidden" in grey. When even that would reveal something, nothing is shown, and counts, searches and totals behave as if the rows were not there. A total that would reveal fewer than a set number of hidden rows is refused |
| Marking | A small label in capitals at the top right of a page or sheet ("CONFIDENTIAL · FINANCE"). It follows the content into every report, export and brief |
| Live state | The first fact on the status line says how current the page is: current, as of a time, catching up, or reconnecting. A page never calls an old result current |
| Situation | One row on Today for one business change. It opens a page: what changed, measured; what it is connected to; what is being done; and the responses allowed |
| Notes and hand-over | In any sheet: notes by named people, and "Give this to" a person. The states are given, seen, done |
| Editing together | "Meera Demo is editing this draft." Open a copy. When two people changed the same record, both values are shown and one is chosen |
| Live session | A panel inside a job that shows the one window an agent is using, with Pause, Take over and Stop always visible. After a person takes over, the agent looks again before it acts |
| Results per item | For one action applied to many things: a table with one row per item and its own result. The list it ran on is named and fixed |
| Out of service | A label on any screen whose engine part is down: "Forecasts are paused. Answers from the books still work." Company, Health shows all of them in one table |
| Approximate | The label on a figure that was made less exact on purpose to protect people, with how much of the allowance is left |

enterpriseRules.text:
## 6. The rules that hold on every enterprise screen

These come from the 18 groups of rules in the inventory. Most already hold on the desktop.

| Rule | How the design keeps it |
|---|---|
| Work is not trapped in a chat | An answer, an investigation, a what-if and a decision are saved things with their own pages. The ask line starts them; it does not hold them |
| What you were looking at survives moving around | The company, the lens, the period and the "as known on" date travel with you from page to page, and show on the line that says where you are. Every page has an address that can be shared inside the company |
| Colour is never the only sign | Squares come with words. Known facts, assumptions and open questions differ by label and position |
| Decoration must not suggest certainty | No scores, no gauges, no single readiness percentage. A chart of thin evidence says how thin |
| Lists and tables come before graphs of relations | Records are browsed as rows. A drawing of links appears only for one path at a time |
| Old screens say they are old | Live state on the status line. After a reconnect the page checks access again before showing anything |
| The same rules on every channel | A phone or a message can never approve what the app would not let that person approve |
| Empty, stale and partial are designed states | Each says what can still be done and what would bring the rest |
| Approvals show the real change | The sheet is built from the prepared request. An agent's message never counts as a person's approval |
| Routine work is not buried in confirmations | What the rules already allow runs without asking. There is no single "autonomous mode" switch; each kind of action has its own |
| Only meaningful changes interrupt | A new row on Today needs a real change. The end of an agent's step is not one |
| Hidden means hidden everywhere | Lists, counts, search, totals and drawings of links all agree |
| Claims stay honest | Supported is said per system and per operation. A part that is not proven is called partial |

customerWindow.text:
## 7. The customer window

In the enterprise version a company's own customers may talk to a service agent by chat, portal, mail, messaging or phone. That surface is not part of the app, and no document sets its look. This design gives it rules and leaves the drawing for later.

- It is the company's surface, not Chausar's. It carries the company's name. It uses the same plain parts: rows, a line to type in, small squares for whose turn it is.
- It says who the customer is talking to: an AI service agent, or a named person.
- It shows whether the customer's identity was checked, and how.
- It shows promises as rows: what was promised and by when.
- A hand-over to a person has two states that are never confused: offered, and accepted by a named person.
- It never shows another customer's data, an internal note, or a figure with no receipt.

The staff side lives in Work, Cases, and the rules for what may be sent, and as whom, live in Trust, Channels.

internalConsoles.text:
## 8. Chausar's own consoles

Seventeen surfaces in the inventory are for Chausar's staff, not for customers: releasing to every customer install, watching health, running an incident, moving an install, and keeping the research on each source system. They belong in a separate internal app built from the same parts. They are listed here so that nothing is lost.

| Console | Holds | Built from |
|---|---|---|
| Operator: installs | Every customer install, its version, its state | A table with a strip per install |
| Operator: releases | A signed release, where it has gone, what the evidence says | A time line down the page; a meter for how far it has rolled out |
| Operator: health | Whether real journeys succeed, with honest gaps when watching fails | Tables and out-of-service labels |
| Operator: incidents | Declaring one, its time line, its close with causes | A time line down the page |
| Operator: upkeep | Settings in force, emergency overrides, database upkeep, capacity, moves, tests of resilience, certificates, clean-up | Tables and rows that open |
| Research: register | Every source system and how far research has got | The coverage board as a table |
| Research: samples | What each sample may be used for; new material held apart | A table with a label per sample |
| Research: claims and experiments | Claims, corrections, experiments that can be repeated | A time line; the receipt |

None of these shows customer content. The final plan says the fleet console "must not become a general cross-customer content store".

caBoundary.text:
## 9. The CA console

![The CA console and the client's own vault](diagrams/ca.svg)

A CA firm with 80 small clients cannot open 80 apps. The console puts a list of clients in front of the same app.

**The rule the design rests on.** Each client's books stay in that client's own vault. The console holds status about each client: dates, counts and states. It holds no figure, no name of a client's customer, and no document. To see figures, the CA opens the client and works inside that client's workspace, with the seat the client gave. This keeps the promise that nothing is read across workspaces, and it means the console can exist without a decision about hosting many businesses together.

![The CA console](pictures/S19-CA-Console.light.png)

**The rail of the console** has six places: Today, Clients, Work, Reports, Tools, Trust. There is no Ask and no Books at the firm's level, because there are no books at that level. Both appear the moment a client is opened.

| Code | Screen | What it shows |
|---|---|---|
| CA-01 | Clients | A table: the client, when its books were last read, the month's close as a strip of four squares (bank, GST, TDS, trial balance), how many things await the firm, and what is due next. Three words filter it: Needs you, Close not done, All. Arrow keys move, Enter opens |
| CA-02 | The firm's Today | What awaits the firm across all clients, grouped by client, as counts. Due dates across all clients from the published calendar |
| CA-03 | Inside a client | The client's own workspace in the Books view, with a banner: "Demo shop, a client of Demo and Co. Back to clients." What the CA can do is set by the seat: a CA seat reads and exports until a date; an accountant seat also prepares, and never approves money |
| CA-04 | Month-end hand-over | Per client, the schedules of the CA pack as a checklist: trial balance, bank reconciliation, the GST match, the TDS match, ageing. Each opens the report page. Export to Excel and to a file Tally can import |
| CA-05 | To co-sign | Proposals from clients' workspaces that an accountant may co-sign: meanings, recipes, account classes. Each is opened inside its client |
| CA-06 | The same step for many clients | One request applied to a chosen list of clients, for example "send the guide for the September GST file". A table with one row per client and its own result |
| CA-07 | The firm's library | Recipes, ready-made jobs and checks the firm reuses across clients. Structure only: no client's data is in it |
| CA-08 | The firm's people | Who in the firm may open which client. A client's owner gives the seat; the firm cannot add itself to a client |
| CA-09 | Invite a client | The one-page guide to forward. A client that has not joined shows "invited, not joined" |
| CA-10 | Questions sent by clients | The "ask a person" files that clients sent when Chausar said not yet, each opened inside its client |
| CA-11 | The firm's name on reports | A setting. The plan's price for firms is per client file, and it is marked "planned" |

**What changes in the parts.** One thing: the strip of small squares, used on the desktop for twelve months of a source, is used here for the four steps of the month's close.

**What is not decided.** No document describes a CA firm. The plan places the console after day 10. Whether a firm's status view runs on the firm's own computer or on a hosted service, and what a client must agree to for its status to be shown there, are the founder's decisions. The design works either way because only status crosses.

openChoices.text:
## 15. What is still open

**Fable's choices that the founder may want to reverse.**

| # | Choice | Reason | The other way |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The pictures are drawn at 1366 by 768, and the smallest supported window is 1024 wide | No review names a size; this is a common old laptop | Pick a size after measuring the test laptop |
| 2 | Chausar's own lines never say "I" | It reads as a tool reporting, not a character talking, which fits "not AI-ish". The plan's sentence "I cannot calculate that yet" becomes "Not yet. No calculation covers this" | Keep "I" for answers only |
| 3 | The fonts are bundled inside the app | The app must not call the network for a font, and the day 1 screens used system fonts only | System fonts, and lose the brand's look |
| 4 | WCAG 2.2 AA as the working target | The final plan asks for a level to be chosen before any claim | Choose another level, or name none yet |
| 5 | Auto-lock after ten minutes without use, as the default | No review gives a time | Any other time |
| 6 | Things the plan puts "in the trust panel" live where the work is, with the rule in Trust (part 5) | A list of jobs is work, not a rule. The four trust questions stay on one screen | Put them all under Trust |
| 7 | Only Today carries a count | One number to watch | A count on every place |
| 8 | No pop-up messages and no system notifications by default. The tray icon shows the count | Quiet, and a message that fades is missed by slow readers and screen readers | Offer system notifications for money and outside messages as a switch |
| 9 | Reports gets a fourth sub-place, Due dates | The compliance calendar needs a home that works with no data connected | Keep it inside The week ahead only |
| 10 | The enterprise version adds an eighth place, Company, and keeps roles, markings and audit under Trust | Trust is about the data; Company is about the installation | Put everything for administrators in one place |
| 11 | The CA console shows status only across clients, never figures | Each client's books stay in that client's vault. The final plan gives every customer a separate place and no document describes a view across them | A hosted view across clients, which needs a tenancy decision |
| 12 | The phone page paired to the desktop is drawn but marked "after day 10" | The plan's own recommendation is a phone app after day 10 | Build it inside the ten days |
| 13 | In the Simple view the rail has four places and the rest sit under More | A shop owner should not face seven doors | Seven places in every view |
| 14 | A what-if is saved under Ask, Saved, with its own label. The full strategy workspace of the enterprise version is a sub-place of Ask called Plans | The seven places have no Strategy place, and a what-if starts as a question | A place of its own |

**Not yet known, and not for the design to settle.**

- The Hindi text needs a native reader before release.
- The names of the three approval tiers and of the daily caps are set on days 7 and 8.
- The speed targets (installer size, import time, answer time) are chosen by the founder from the bench's numbers.
- How a phone pairs with the desktop, and who owns the WhatsApp number in each plan.
- Whether a new recovery kit can be issued, and whether recovery resets the passphrase.
- The pages of the website that belong to the release (download, pricing, the CA sign-up) are in the website's own repository and are not designed here.

**What this design does not cover.** Chausar's own operator console and research console are listed in the enterprise file with the parts they would use, but not drawn. Customer-facing channels of the enterprise version (a company's own customers talking to a service agent) are given rules and a place for the staff side, not screens.
